clue.text: Using muscle, an active America

indicators.note: active suggests letters busily moving about, so the words muscle and an are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flexes their muscles in an energetic, very American way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'active' is the anagram signal working on MUSCLE and AN; 'Using' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The personification of the United States government and nation is the bearded figure in a top hat.

clue.text: Crazy type, one going to bolt

definitions.meaning: an eccentric or madcap person
the threaded piece screwed onto a bolt

explanation.surface: A madman is about to run off.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a madcap person, and also the small threaded fastener that pairs with a bolt.

clue.text: Weapon held up by a corporal?

definitions.meaning: a long spear carried by a mounted knight
the word placed before corporal names a junior army rank, so it holds the corporal up

explanation.surface: A soldier raises his spear.
explanation.walkthrough: A lance corporal is the lowest non-commissioned rank in the British Army; the weapon's name comes first, 'holding up' the corporal.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight's long spear-like weapon, and also the first word of a British army rank.

clue.text: Snap mother cleverly with this?

indicators.note: cleverly suggests a smart reworking, so the letters of snap mother are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion for taking a neat photo of Mum on your phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleverly' rearranges SNAP MOTHER, and the whole clue also describes the device you would photograph her with.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile phone with a camera is what most people now use to take a quick snapshot.

clue.text: Sprayer's title?

definitions.meaning: a device that sprays a fine mist, with the apostrophe s read as is
the form of address used before a man's surname

explanation.surface: A query about what to call the person doing the spraying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that produces fine droplets is literally a mist-maker, and the same word is a man's courtesy form of address.

clue.text: Plaguey creature not to be found when copper intervenes

indicators.note: intervenes means comes between, so the copper symbol is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: something missing and not to be found is lost
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A pest vanishes when the police officer steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical element, CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming insects of this kind formed one of the ten biblical plagues of Egypt.

clue.text: Where to go miles and appear out of the fog

parts.note: the loo is the British slang word for the toilet, where one goes

explanation.surface: Directions to walk some miles until something emerges from the mist.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is everyday British slang for a toilet, 'where to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into view as a large, vague, threatening shape, as through mist.

clue.text: Eccentric testimonial

definitions.meaning: an odd, colourful person
a reference letter vouching for someone's qualities

explanation.surface: A strange reference letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddball person is one, and an old word for a written reference from an employer is the same.

clue.text: As poet, seek a phrase to fit

indicators.note: a fit is a convulsion, so the words seek a phrase are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to a poet hunting for the right words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fit' looks like matching words but signals the anagram of SEEK A PHRASE; 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bard of Avon is the best-known English dramatist and sonnet writer.

clue.text: Laurel's speaking a bit of poetry

indicators.note: speaking means the words are said aloud and spelt to match the sound

parts.note: Stan Laurel of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy, so Laurel's is said as Stan's

explanation.surface: A comedian recites some verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' turns Stan's (Laurel's first name plus 's) into the sound STANZ, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A verse of a poem is a group of lines forming one unit.

clue.text: One not having paid to travel, bailiffs finally take vehicle to pound

definitions.text: One not having paid to travel

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word bailiffs

parts.note: a car is towed away when it is taken to the police pound

explanation.surface: Bailiffs end up impounding the car of someone who dodged the fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A person hiding aboard a ship or plane travels without buying a ticket.

clue.text: A number noticed, happening to enter

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes into the other, here the occurrence goes inside

parts.note: something noticed has been seen
a happening is an event

explanation.surface: A figure was spotted as something occurred.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten plus seven is simply one of the whole numbers.

clue.text: Fly-by-night, showing more mph, tore off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong or astray, so more mph and tore are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shady character speeds off, going faster and faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly-by-night' looks like a shifty person but means a creature that flies at night; 'off' rearranges MORE MPH TORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large silk moth that flies at night, so literally a night flyer.

clue.text: Make statement about Vulcan being monotonous

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, so the setter's pronoun sits within the verb

parts.note: to make a statement is to say
Vulcan is this puzzle's setter, so the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A dull speech about the Roman god of fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Vulcan looks like the Roman god but is this puzzle's setter; setters refer to themselves as 'me', which 'about' wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for repetitive and lacking variety, all much alike.

clue.text: Such income not permanent?

definitions.meaning: the money left to spend after tax is described by this word
something meant to be thrown away after use

explanation.surface: A question about whether a certain kind of earnings will last.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare post-tax earnings are called this, and throwaway single-use items are too.

clue.text: Pledge is quiet and frivolous

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical term for quiet
light-hearted or trivial, as in light entertainment

explanation.surface: A promise that is soft-spoken and not very serious.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb meaning to promise solemnly, as in plighting one's troth.

clue.text: Life so turbulent to staff here?

indicators.note: turbulent means agitated and churning, so life so is rearranged

parts.note: to staff a place is to man it

explanation.surface: Wondering where a stormy life might lead to the hiring of workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' rearranges LIFE SO only; the Irish Sea island is a British Crown dependency.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-governing island in the Irish Sea, offered as the place in question.

clue.text: Recommend toy as excellent

parts.note: to tip something is to recommend it as a likely winner
a spinning top is a child's toy

explanation.surface: Endorsing a plaything as first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal, old-fashioned British term for first-class or of the highest quality.

clue.text: Judicial decision-making lines on page

definitions.meaning: a judgment handed down by a court
drawing straight lines across paper, as with a ruler

explanation.surface: A court's process for reaching judgments, set down in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's pronouncement is one, and the act of drawing straight guide lines on paper is the same word.

clue.text: Greek state once displayed paintings in Bath, say

indicators.note: in places the pictures piece within the resort town

parts.note: Bath is an English spa town, so it is an example of a spa
paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek state exhibits pictures in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a Somerset city famous for its Roman hot springs, hence a SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek city-state famed for its warriors, long since gone.

clue.text: Mentioning hair band, sounded like an ass

indicators.note: mentioning means the word is spoken, so the spelling follows its sound

parts.note: a braid is a plait or band of hair

explanation.surface: Someone who talks about their hairband sounds foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's harsh cry is a bray, so making that noise means this past tense verb.

clue.text: Criminal's held by bishop

definitions.meaning: a villain or lawbreaker
a bishop carries a hooked staff, the crozier

explanation.surface: A villain is detained by a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a lawbreaker, and also the shepherd's hooked staff a bishop carries.

clue.text: Angry about a style of music

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry
over can mean about, as in arguing over something

explanation.surface: Someone furious about a musical genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Music blending genres, such as classical with pop, so it reaches a wider audience.

clue.text: Where skaters are suspended

definitions.meaning: skaters glide on a frozen surface
put on hold, postponed for later

explanation.surface: A question of where skaters are hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally standing on frozen water, and as an idiom meaning postponed or kept in reserve.

clue.text: Clubs put down surface for tennis

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
to lay something is to put it down

explanation.surface: Tennis clubs lay a new court surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Courts at the French Open are made of this earthy material.

clue.text: Classmate, in official style

definitions.meaning: split into class and mate, a school form plus an ally
done in a proper, ceremonious way

explanation.surface: A school friend behaving in an official manner.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a class is called a FORM; read Classmate as FORM + ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: This adverb means according to proper conventions or etiquette.

clue.text: Issues instructions for underwear

definitions.meaning: gives someone a briefing, as a verb
short close-fitting underpants

explanation.surface: Someone hands out directions on what underwear to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for giving people a briefing and a plural noun for snug pants.

clue.text: Enemy of international environmental group

definitions.meaning: an opponent or adversary
Friends of the Earth, the green campaigning organisation, by its initials

explanation.surface: An opponent of a worldwide green organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: An adversary, and also the initials of the campaigning group Friends of the Earth.

clue.text: Nervous about insect in hut

indicators.note: about means going round, so the timid word wraps the insect

parts.note: shy means timid or nervous
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Someone is jittery about a bug in their shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A crude, roughly built shack or cabin.

clue.text: Got lower in part of pool, conserving energy

indicators.note: conserving means keeping something within, so the energy symbol is held inside

parts.note: the deep end of a swimming pool
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone sank lower in the deep section of the pool while saving their strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To make or become further down is to increase in depth.
